title: Former 'Baywatch' Actress Alexandra Paul Arrested For Freeing Dogs During Animal Rights Protest - NewsBreak
text:
By Baila Eve Zisman ,
12 hours ago Former Baywatch star Alexandra Paul was arrested for trespassing on March 15 after participating in efforts to free dogs from a controversial breeding facility.
Paul, 62, was taken into custody in Blue Mounds, Wisconsin, after she and a group of between 50 and 60 protestors trespassed on the Ridglan Farms property at about 8:30 a.m. Approximately 20 people were arrested.
>50 ‘BEST’ CELEBRITY MUGSHOTS & THE STORIES BEHIND THEM!
Ridglan Farms is one of two large dog breeders in the United States that offer beagles for scientific research experimentation. In October 2025, the La Crosse County District Attorney and Ridglan Farms agreed that the facility would no longer operate under its Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection license, and starting July 1, 2026, would no longer sell dogs bred for biomedical research.
According to the Dane County Sheriff’s Office, on March 15, “some activists broke into the facility and began removing numerous dogs.”
“Some of the beagles taken were recovered and returned to Ridglan Farms, but several beagles remain unaccounted for.”

In a statement, Sheriff Kalvin Barrett declared, “The Dane County Sheriff’s Office understands how deeply people feel for the beagles at Ridglan Farms, and we respect their right to express that passion through peaceful protests… Our role is to keep everyone safe and to respond when unlawful activity takes place.”
He added, “We encourage anyone with concerns about animal welfare or research practices to engage through lawful and constructive avenues.”
In almost four decades of activism, Paul has been arrested dozens of times for civil disobedience. She was most recently charged with misdemeanor theft after she allegedly took two chickens from a Foster Farms truck in September 2021. She testified in March 2023 and was found not guilty.
Paul has long been a vocal animal rights activist, telling People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) in 2011 that she wrote in her acting contracts that she refused to wear “any makeup tested on animals,” and did not wear fur, leather, wool or silk.
She is still best known for her role as Stephanie Holden on Baywatch from 1992 to 1997.
